tracks.title: Foundations
tracks.blurb: Start here. Greetings, who you are, what you speak, having, liking, living, and wanting - the backbone of everything.

lessons.title: Warm-up - greetings
lessons.note: Everything you have already seen. Read it out loud. Tap a sentence to hear it, double-tap a word for its meaning, or drag across a few.

paragraphs.en: Hello!
My name is Jorik.
What is your name?
How are you?

t.g: (turns a sentence into a yes/no question)

paragraphs.en: I am very well.
I am okay.
I am not very well.
And you?
Thanks!

lessons.title: Text 1 - who speaks Chinese
lessons.note: New words appear woven into what you know. Do not memorise - just read.

paragraphs.en: My name is Xiaolin.
I am Chinese.
Your name is Jorik.
You are not Chinese.
You are British.
Xiaolin is Chinese.
Xiaolin speaks Chinese.
Jorik is British.
Jorik also speaks Chinese.
Jorik speaks a little Chinese.
He does not speak much Chinese, but he speaks a little.
Xiaolin speaks a lot of Chinese.
He is Chinese!

lessons.title: Text 2 - teacher and student
lessons.note: New here: lǎoshī, xuésheng, de. They repeat many times on purpose.

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin is a teacher.
She is a Chinese teacher.
She is a very good teacher.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Jorik is a student.
He is not a teacher.
He is Xiaolin's student.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin is Jorik's teacher.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Jorik is Xiaolin's student.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin says: "How are you?"

t.g: (turns a sentence into a yes/no question)

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "I am very well. And you?"
Xiaolin says: "I am very well too."
Jorik speaks a little Chinese.
Xiaolin says: "Your Chinese is very good!"

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "Thanks! But I speak a little. I do not speak much."
Xiaolin says: "A little is very good. A little is also Chinese!"

lessons.title: Text 3 - I don't understand
lessons.note: New here: Yīngwén, míngbai, yìsi. Notice how 'shénme yìsi?' means 'what does it mean?'.

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin is a teacher.
She speaks Chinese, and she also speaks a little English.
Jorik is a student.
He speaks English, and he also speaks a little Chinese.
Xiaolin speaks Chinese.
Jorik does not understand.
Jorik says: "I do not understand. What does it mean?"
Xiaolin speaks English.
Jorik understands.
Jorik says: "Ah, I understand!"
Xiaolin says: "You are a very good student."

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "Thanks, teacher."

lessons.title: Check - answer shì or bú shì
lessons.note: Read each question. Answer out loud with shì (yes) or bú shì (no).

paragraphs.en: Is Xiaolin Chinese?

t.g: (turns a sentence into a yes/no question)

paragraphs.en: Is Jorik Chinese?

t.g: (turns a sentence into a yes/no question)

paragraphs.en: Is Xiaolin a student?

t.g: (turns a sentence into a yes/no question)

paragraphs.en: Is Jorik Xiaolin's teacher?

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)
(turns a sentence into a yes/no question)

lessons.title: Text 4 - friends
lessons.note: New here: yǒu / méiyǒu (have / not have), péngyou, hé, dōu, tāmen.

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin has a friend.
Her friend is called Wang Mei.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Wang Mei is also a teacher.
Xiaolin and Wang Mei are both teachers.
They are very good friends.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Jorik also has a friend.
His friend is called Tom.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Tom is British.
Tom does not speak Chinese.
Tom does not have a Chinese teacher.
Jorik has a Chinese teacher.
Jorik says: "I have a teacher, but you do not have a teacher."
Tom says: "I do not have a teacher, but I have you! You are my Chinese teacher."

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "I am not a teacher! I am a student. I speak a little Chinese, I do not speak much."

lessons.title: Text 5 - where people live
lessons.note: New here: zhù (live), zài (at / in), nǎr (where), Běijīng, Lúndūn.

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin lives in Beijing.
Beijing is in China.
Jorik lives in London.
London is in Britain.
Wang Mei says: "Where does Jorik live?"
Xiaolin says: "He lives in London."
Wang Mei says: "Where is London?"
Xiaolin says: "London is in Britain. London is not in China."
Tom also lives in London.
Jorik and Tom both live in London; they both live in Britain.
Xiaolin and Wang Mei both live in Beijing; they are both Chinese.
Jorik does not live in Beijing, but his teacher lives in Beijing.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

lessons.title: Text 6 - likes and reasons
lessons.note: New here: xǐhuan (like), wèishénme (why), yīnwèi (because), nán, cài, hǎochī.

paragraphs.en: Jorik likes Chinese.
He likes Chinese a lot.
Tom says: "Why do you like Chinese?"
Jorik says: "Because Chinese is very interesting."
Tom says: "But Chinese is very hard!"
Jorik says: "Right, Chinese is very hard. Very hard, but very interesting."
Jorik also likes Chinese food.
He says: "Chinese food is very tasty."
Tom does not like Chinese food.
Tom likes British food.
Jorik says: "British food is not tasty!"
Tom says: "I do not understand. Why is it not tasty?"
Jorik says: "Because I am British, I know."

lessons.title: Text 7 - wanting to go to China
lessons.note: The longest yet. New here: měitiān, xuéxí, xiǎng, qù, lái, wǒmen, chī, and the phrase 'qǐng zài shuō yí biàn' (please say it again).

paragraphs.en: Jorik studies Chinese every day.
Every day!
He really likes studying Chinese.
Xiaolin is in Beijing, Jorik is in London, but they speak Chinese every day.
Xiaolin says: "Do you want to go to China?"

t.g: to want to, would like to
(turns a sentence into a yes/no question)

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "I really want to go to China! I want to go to Beijing."

t.g: to want to, would like to
to want to, would like to

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin says: "Why do you want to go to Beijing?"

t.g: to want to, would like to

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "Because you live in Beijing, because Beijing has many Chinese people, and because Beijing has very tasty food."

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin says: "Good! You come to Beijing, we eat Chinese food."
Jorik says: "But my Chinese is not good. In Beijing, I do not understand Chinese people. They speak a lot, I speak a little."

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin says: "No problem. You say: 'I do not understand. Please say it once more.' Chinese people are very nice, they will say it again."
Jorik says: "Good. I understand now."
Xiaolin says: "Your Chinese is very good. You are a very good student."

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)
('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

lessons.title: Check - answer in English
lessons.note: Read each question and answer in English in your head. No output pressure yet.

paragraphs.en: Does Tom have a Chinese teacher?

t.g: (turns a sentence into a yes/no question)

paragraphs.en: Where does Xiaolin live?
Why does Jorik like Chinese?
Who does not like Chinese food?
Where does Jorik want to go? Why?

t.g: to want to, would like to

tracks.title: Numbers & age
tracks.blurb: Zero to thirty-five, the counting word ge, and asking how old someone is.

lessons.title: One to ten
lessons.note: New: the numbers yī to shí, líng (zero), ge (the everyday counting word), and liǎng (the 'two' you use before ge). Read them out loud.

paragraphs.en: One, two, three, four, five.
Six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
Zero.
I have one friend.
I have two friends.

t.g: (the everyday counting word: sān ge rén)

paragraphs.en: I have three friends.

t.g: (the everyday counting word: sān ge rén)

paragraphs.en: Jorik has three friends.

t.g: (the everyday counting word: sān ge rén)

paragraphs.en: One is Chinese, two are British.

t.g: (the everyday counting word: sān ge rén)

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin has many students.
Tom does not have a Chinese friend; he does not have a single one.

lessons.title: How old are you?
lessons.note: New: suì (years old), jǐ (how many, for small numbers), dà / xiǎo (big / small, also old / young), and the bigger numbers shíbā, èrshí, èrshíbā, sānshí, sānshíwǔ.

paragraphs.en: Ten, eleven, twelve.
Eighteen, twenty, twenty-eight.
Thirty, thirty-five.
Xiaolin says: "How old are you?"
Jorik says: "I am thirty years old. And you?"
Xiaolin says: "I am thirty-five years old."
Tom is twenty-eight years old.
Jorik is thirty; Tom is twenty-eight.
Jorik is older, Tom is younger.

lessons.title: Check - numbers
lessons.note: Read each question and answer out loud. Use liǎng (not èr) before ge.

paragraphs.en: How old are you?
How many friends do you have?

t.g: (the everyday counting word: sān ge rén)

paragraphs.en: Is Xiaolin thirty-five?

t.g: (turns a sentence into a yes/no question)

paragraphs.en: How old is Xiaolin?

tracks.title: Family & home
tracks.blurb: Your family: parents, brothers and sisters, how many, how old, and where they live.

lessons.title: My family
lessons.note: New: jiā (home / family), bàba, māma, gēge. 'wǒ jiā yǒu ... ge rén' = 'in my family there are ... people'.

paragraphs.en: In my family there are four people.

t.g: (the everyday counting word: sān ge rén)

paragraphs.en: Dad, mum, older brother, and me.
I have one older brother.
My older brother is British.
My dad and mum both live in London.
Xiaolin says: "How many people are in your family?"

t.g: (the everyday counting word: sān ge rén)

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "In my family there are four people."

t.g: (the everyday counting word: sān ge rén)

lessons.title: Brothers and sisters
lessons.note: New: dìdi, jiějie, mèimei. Ages come back here - dà / xiǎo also mean older / younger.

paragraphs.en: I have an older brother and a younger sister.
I do not have a younger brother.
My older brother is twenty, my younger sister is eighteen.
My older brother is older, my younger sister is younger.
They are both students.
Wang Mei has an older sister.
Her older sister is a teacher too.
Wang Mei and her older sister both live in Beijing.

lessons.title: Whose family
lessons.note: Everything so far, woven together: who is in the family, how old they are, where they live, and what they do.

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin says: "Is your dad Chinese?"

t.g: (turns a sentence into a yes/no question)

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "No, my dad is British. My whole family is British."
Jorik's mum is a teacher.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: She is an English teacher, but she also speaks a little Chinese.
Jorik really likes his family.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: He says: "My family is small, but very good."

tracks.title: Food & drink
tracks.blurb: Eating and drinking: what you want, what is tasty, and ordering a meal.

lessons.title: What do you drink?
lessons.note: New: hē (drink), yào (want / order), chá, kāfēi, shuǐ, kě (thirsty), hǎohē (nice to drink).

paragraphs.en: I drink tea.
I like drinking tea.
Chinese tea is very nice.
Tom says: "What do you want to drink?"

t.g: to want to, would like to

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "I am thirsty. I want water."

t.g: to want, to need, to order

paragraphs.en: Tom does not drink tea; he drinks coffee.
He drinks a lot of coffee every day.

lessons.title: What do you eat?
lessons.note: New: è (hungry), mǐfàn, miàn, ròu, yú, jīdàn. chī and hǎochī come back.

paragraphs.en: I am hungry.
I want to eat noodles.

t.g: to want to, would like to

paragraphs.en: Chinese noodles are very tasty.
Xiaolin says: "What do you want to eat?"

t.g: to want to, would like to

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "I want rice, fish, and an egg."

t.g: to want, to need, to order

paragraphs.en: Tom does not eat fish.
He eats meat; he really likes meat.
He says: "Fish is not tasty, meat is tasty!"

lessons.title: Ordering food
lessons.note: Put it together: at a meal, saying what you are, what you want, and thanking. yào here means 'to order'.

paragraphs.en: Jorik and Tom are hungry.
They want to eat Chinese food.

t.g: to want to, would like to

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "I want rice and fish. I want tea too."

t.g: to want, to need, to order
to want, to need, to order

paragraphs.en: Tom says: "I want noodles and meat. I do not want fish."

t.g: to want, to need, to order
to want, to need, to order

paragraphs.en: The Chinese food is very tasty.
Jorik says: "This is really tasty. Thanks!"

tracks.title: Every day
tracks.blurb: Today and tomorrow, telling the time, and a walk through a whole day from morning to night.

lessons.title: Today and tomorrow
lessons.note: New: jīntiān (today), míngtiān (tomorrow), zuótiān (yesterday).

paragraphs.en: Today I study Chinese.
Yesterday I also studied Chinese.
I study Chinese every day.
Xiaolin says: "What do you want to do tomorrow?"

t.g: to want to, would like to

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "Tomorrow I want to eat Chinese food with you."

t.g: to want to, would like to

paragraphs.en: Today Tom is hungry, tomorrow Tom wants to eat noodles.

t.g: to want to, would like to

lessons.title: What time is it?
lessons.note: New: xiànzài (now), diǎn (o'clock), bàn (half past). 'xiànzài jǐ diǎn?' = 'what time is it now?'. Remember: 2 o'clock is liǎng diǎn.

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "What time is it now?"
Tom says: "It is seven o'clock now."
Now it is eight o'clock.
Now it is half past eight.
Now it is two o'clock.
At twelve o'clock Jorik eats.
At eleven o'clock at night he sleeps.

lessons.title: My day
lessons.note: The longest here. New: zǎoshang, shàngwǔ, xiàwǔ, wǎnshang, qǐchuáng (get up), shuìjiào (sleep), gōngzuò (work), kàn (read / watch), shū (book).

paragraphs.en: Every day Jorik gets up at seven in the morning.
In the morning he studies Chinese.
He really likes studying Chinese.
In the afternoon Jorik works.
His mum works too.
In the evening he drinks tea and reads a book.
He reads Chinese books.
Chinese books are hard, but very interesting.
At eleven at night he sleeps.
He says: "I am going to sleep now. Goodnight!"

t.g: to want, to need, to order

tracks.title: Places & directions
tracks.blurb: Shops, schools, restaurants and hospitals: where things are, and how you get there.

lessons.title: Places in town
lessons.note: New: shāngdiàn (shop), xuéxiào (school), fànguǎn (restaurant), yīyuàn (hospital). Use zài (at / in) to say where someone is.

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin is a teacher; she is at the school.
The school is in Beijing.
Jorik is hungry; he is at the restaurant.
The restaurant's food is very tasty.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Tom is at the shop.
He wants to drink coffee, but the shop has no coffee.

t.g: to want to, would like to

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin's mum works at the hospital.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

lessons.title: Where is it?
lessons.note: New: lǐ (inside - 'X lǐ' means 'in X') and pángbiān (next to). 'zài nǎr?' comes back.

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin says: "Where is Jorik?"
Tom says: "He is inside the school."
Jorik says: "Where is the tea?"
Tom says: "The tea is in the shop."
Wang Mei says: "Where is the restaurant?"
Xiaolin says: "The restaurant is next to the school."

lessons.title: Going places
lessons.note: New: zǒulù (to walk, on foot), zuò chē (to go by car / bus), chē (vehicle), yuǎn (far), jìn (near).

paragraphs.en: Jorik wants to go to the restaurant.

t.g: to want to, would like to

paragraphs.en: The restaurant is near; he walks there.

t.g: to walk, to go on foot

paragraphs.en: Jorik wants to go to the school.

t.g: to want to, would like to

paragraphs.en: The school is far; he goes by car.

t.g: to sit; to travel by (zuò chē)

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin walks to school every day.

t.g: to walk, to go on foot

paragraphs.en: She likes walking.

t.g: to walk, to go on foot

tracks.title: Shopping & money
tracks.blurb: Buying things, asking the price, and whether something is expensive or cheap.

lessons.title: Buying things
lessons.note: New: mǎi (to buy), zhège (this one), nàge (that one).

paragraphs.en: Jorik is at the shop; he wants to buy tea.

t.g: to want to, would like to

paragraphs.en: He says: "I want this one."

t.g: to want, to need, to order

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin buys coffee; Tom buys water.
This one is tea, that one is coffee.

lessons.title: How much?
lessons.note: New: duōshao (how much), qián (money), kuài (yuan). 'duōshao qián?' = 'how much money?'.

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "How much is this one?"
The shopkeeper says: "This tea is five yuan."
That coffee is thirty yuan.
Jorik says: "I want the tea. Here is five yuan. Thanks!"

t.g: to want, to need, to order

lessons.title: Expensive or cheap
lessons.note: New: guì (expensive), piányi (cheap).

paragraphs.en: The coffee is expensive; the tea is cheap.
Jorik says: "The coffee is too expensive, I do not want it."

t.g: to want, to need, to order

paragraphs.en: Tea is cheap and nice to drink; Jorik wants tea.

t.g: to want, to need, to order

paragraphs.en: Tom says: "British food is expensive, and it is not tasty!"

tracks.title: Colours & things
tracks.blurb: Colours, and describing objects: new or old, and nice to look at.

lessons.title: Colours
lessons.note: New: yánsè (colour) and hóngsè, lánsè, báisè, hēisè (red, blue, white, black).

paragraphs.en: I like red.
Xiaolin says: "What colour do you like?"
Tom likes blue; Xiaolin likes white.
Coffee is black; tea is not black.

lessons.title: Describing things
lessons.note: New: xīn (new), jiù (old), hǎokàn (nice-looking). 'hóngsè de shū' = 'a red book'.

paragraphs.en: Jorik's book is red.

('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: The old book is not nice.

lessons.title: Which one?
lessons.note: New: háishì (or, in a question). 'A háishì B?' asks you to choose.

paragraphs.en: This one is a red book, that one is a blue book.

tracks.title: Weather & seasons
tracks.blurb: Hot and cold, rain, and the four seasons.

lessons.title: Today's weather
lessons.note: New: tiānqì (weather), rè (hot), lěng (cold).

paragraphs.en: Today the weather is very good.
Today it is very hot.
Beijing is hot; London is cold.
Today Beijing's weather is very hot.

lessons.title: Rain
lessons.note: New: xiàyǔ (to rain).

paragraphs.en: Today it is raining.
Jorik says: "I do not like rain."
Tomorrow it will not rain; the weather will be good.
When it rains, Jorik reads at home.

lessons.title: The seasons
lessons.note: New: chūntiān, xiàtiān, qiūtiān, dōngtiān (spring, summer, autumn, winter).

paragraphs.en: Spring is not hot and not cold.
Summer is very hot.
Winter is very cold; Beijing is very cold in winter.
Jorik likes autumn; autumn is not hot and not cold.

tracks.title: Days & dates
tracks.blurb: Days of the week, months, dates, and birthdays.

lessons.title: Days of the week
lessons.note: New: xīngqī (week) and the days xīngqīyī to xīngqītiān. Read them out loud.

paragraphs.en: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday.
Thursday, Friday.
Saturday, Sunday.

lessons.title: What day is it?
lessons.note: New: 'jīntiān xīngqī jǐ?' = 'what day is it today?'.

paragraphs.en: Jorik says: "What day is it today?"
Xiaolin says: "Today is Wednesday."
Tomorrow is Thursday.
On Saturday and Sunday I do not work.

lessons.title: Months and dates
lessons.note: New: yuè (month), hào (day of the month), shēngrì (birthday). Numbers make the dates: 'sān yuè shí hào' = March 10th.

paragraphs.en: It is January now.
Today is the fifth.
Jorik's birthday is March tenth.

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin says: "When is your birthday?"

t.g: ('s / of - links a describer to a noun)

tracks.title: Hobbies
tracks.blurb: Sport, music and films - and talking about your weekend.

lessons.title: What do you like to do?
lessons.note: New: dǎ (play a ball game), qiú (ball), lánqiú (basketball), tī (kick), zúqiú (football).

paragraphs.en: Jorik likes to play basketball.

t.g: to play (a ball game), to hit

paragraphs.en: Tom likes to play football.
Xiaolin says: "Do you like playing ball?"

t.g: to play (a ball game), to hit
(turns a sentence into a yes/no question)

paragraphs.en: Jorik plays basketball every day.

t.g: to play (a ball game), to hit

lessons.title: Music and films
lessons.note: New: tīng (listen), yīnyuè (music), chàng (sing), gē (song), diànyǐng (film).

paragraphs.en: Xiaolin likes to listen to music.
She also likes to sing.
Jorik likes to watch films.
He watches Chinese films; they are very interesting.

lessons.title: The weekend
lessons.note: New: yóuyǒng (to swim). Days of the week come back (see the Days & dates track).

paragraphs.en: On Saturday Jorik plays basketball.

t.g: to play (a ball game), to hit

paragraphs.en: On Sunday he watches a film and listens to music.
Tom likes swimming; he swims every day.
Xiaolin says: "What do you like to do?"

tracks.title: Feelings & body
tracks.blurb: Happy, tired, busy, and saying when you are unwell.

lessons.title: How do you feel?
lessons.note: New: gāoxìng (happy), lèi (tired), máng (busy).

paragraphs.en: Today I am very happy.
Jorik studies every day; he is very busy.
In the evening he is very tired.
He is tired, but he is happy.

lessons.title: Not feeling well
lessons.note: New: tóu (head), téng (to ache), bìng (to be ill), shūfu (comfortable; bù shūfu = unwell).

paragraphs.en: Tom is unwell today.
His head aches.
He is ill; he is at the hospital.
Xiaolin says: "No problem. Drink a little water."

lessons.title: Tired but happy
lessons.note: Everything together: study, feelings, and being a good student.

paragraphs.en: Jorik studies Chinese every day; he is tired, but very happy.
He says: "Chinese is hard, but I am happy."
Xiaolin is happy too.
She says: "You are a very good student."

to walk, to go on foot
